clue.text: Freelance writer retained by editor during shift to the right

indicators.note: during says the next piece sits within the span of the shift word

parts.note: to indent text is to shift it to the right of the margin

indicators.note: something retained by another is held inside it

parts.note: a pen is a writing implement, hence a writer

explanation.surface: A freelance journalist's copy is kept by an editor while the paper drifts politically rightwards.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface's 'shift to the right' sounds political, but it is the typesetting sense: indenting a line moves it right of the margin. 'retained by' builds EPEND, which 'during' places inside the indent word.
explanation.definitionFit: A freelance works for no single employer, being self-employed and unattached.

clue.text: Sort of informal antonym that's anything but provocative

indicators.note: sort is read as a verb, so the following words are to be sorted into a fresh order

explanation.surface: A grammarian describes a casual opposite word that could never cause offence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sort of' looks like a vague hedge, but 'sort' is the anagram signal working on the fifteen letters of 'informal antonym'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something calm and unlikely to stir up anger is the very reverse of provocative.

clue.text: Three Mobile number

indicators.note: mobile means able to move about, so the letters of the word are rearranged

explanation.surface: A phone number on the Three mobile network.
explanation.walkthrough: Three is a UK mobile phone network, which is the surface reading; 'number' is read as 'something that numbs'.
explanation.definitionFit: This old anaesthetic numbs a patient, making it a numbing agent in the crossword's punning sense.

clue.text: Poles initially joined city to their west

parts.note: the south pole's initial S is spelt out as the letter name ess
the north pole's initial N, spelt out as the letter name en, is joined on

explanation.surface: Polish settlers first banded together and then founded a city further west.
explanation.walkthrough: The two poles are S and N, and their initials are written out as the letter names ESS and EN. 'their' refers back to the Poles: this German city lies west of Poland.
explanation.definitionFit: This industrial Ruhr city in Germany lies west of Poland, so it is a city to the Poles' west.

clue.text: See Elgar's first and second resurrected, with name becoming current

indicators.note: one letter becoming another means it is swapped out for it
in a down entry something resurrected rises up, so the letters read from bottom to top
first picks only the opening letter of the composer's name

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Look at Elgar's first and second symphonies being revived with a new title.
explanation.walkthrough: E plus SECOND is reversed by 'resurrected' to give DNOCESE, then 'with name becoming current' changes the N to I.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's seat and, by extension, the area under a bishop's authority.

clue.text: Jaguar, maybe eating wild iguana? On the contrary, they're both here

indicators.note: one thing eating another holds it inside
this reverses the eating just stated, so the lizard's letters swallow the car rather than the other way round
wild signals that the letters run riot into a new order

parts.note: a Jaguar is a make of car, so this is a car by example

explanation.surface: A jaguar devours a wild iguana, or rather the reverse, in their shared Central American habitat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On the contrary' flips the eating: the lizard's jumbled letters (NIAGUA, from 'wild') swallow the car. 'Jaguar' is the big cat in the surface but a car marque in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Both the jaguar and the iguana are native to this Central American country, where both animals live.

clue.text: Cryptically, it could be Mike and Heather from the previous clue?

definitions.text: Cryptically, it could be Mike and Heather from the previous clue?

parts.words: Cryptically, it could be Mike and Heather from the previous clue?
parts.note: Mike is M in the NATO alphabet and heather is erica; together they form the middle letters of a word for people of that region, while a couple from the previous clue's country belong to that region

explanation.surface: A couple named Mike and Heather come from the country in the clue before.
explanation.walkthrough: Two readings: people from Nicaragua are from this region, and M plus ERICA (heather's botanical name) is literally the central stretch of the second word.
explanation.definitionFit: Nicaraguans live on the isthmus between Mexico and Colombia, so they are natives of that region.

clue.text: Organ of holy man stolen from believer

indicators.note: something stolen from a word is taken out of it

parts.note: a theist is one who believes in God
ST, short for saint, is a holy man

explanation.surface: A saint's relic organ has been stolen from a devout believer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests a body part, but here it means a newspaper: the i is the Independent's sister paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A newspaper is called an organ, as a medium of communication; this title is a British daily.

clue.text: Some brain activity, but ultimately not conscious

parts.note: though can mean but, as in 'nice, though dear'

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: A neurologist notes some activity in the brain, though the patient is not conscious.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas and reflections are the product of mental activity in the brain.

clue.text: Move very slowly along island

definitions.meaning: to creep forward a little at a time
in Scotland and Ireland the word is used for a small island, as in Inchcolm

explanation.surface: Someone creeps slowly along a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means edge forward bit by bit; the Scottish noun names a small isle.

clue.text: Long-suffering wife's second to enter incomplete family

indicators.note: a letter that enters a word goes inside it
incomplete means the word loses its final letter

parts.note: stock means family line or ancestry

indicators.note: this picks the second letter of the spouse word

explanation.surface: A patient wife has to become part of a family that is not quite whole.
explanation.definitionFit: A stoic person endures hardship without complaint, as a long-suffering one does.

clue.text: Rodent disease detected in a child's stomach

indicators.note: something detected in a place is found inside it
the stomach is the middle of the body, so this takes the middle letter of the word

parts.note: gout is a disease that inflames the joints

explanation.surface: A doctor finds an illness in a child's belly.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letter of 'child' is I, so A and I surround GOUT.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a burrowing South American rodent related to the guinea pig.

clue.text: Cross the line and briefly gather round circle

indicators.note: one piece placed round another surrounds it
briefly means cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to gather is to infer, as in 'I gather you agree'
a ring is a circle

explanation.surface: Instructions to step over a boundary and quickly form a ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To violate a rule or right is to cross a line that should not be crossed.

clue.text: Girl undressed by alpha male

indicators.note: undressed means stripped of its outer layer, so the outside letters go

parts.note: alpha is A in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A young woman is stripped by a dominant man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'alpha male' reads as one phrase, but 'alpha' is wordplay and 'male' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ira is a man's given name, as in the lyricist Ira Gershwin.

clue.text: Eastern port's drop locks failing to close

parts.note: the possessive ending supplies its letter
to drop someone from a gallows is to hang them

indicators.note: failing to close means the last letter is missing

parts.note: locks are hair

explanation.surface: An Eastern port is described by hair falling short of its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: This Chinese city is one of the world's busiest seaports, in the East.

clue.text: Power possessed by sex symbol of Canada?

indicators.note: a thing possessed by another is held within it

parts.note: male is one of the sexes
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A Canadian heart-throb is said to wield power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sex symbol' reads as a celebrity, but 'sex' is wordplay and 'symbol of Canada?' the definition, the question mark flagging an example.
explanation.definitionFit: The leaf of this tree is on Canada's national flag, making it a national emblem.

clue.text: Spying aids of spies covering deception up

indicators.note: one piece covering another goes round it

parts.note: moles are spies planted inside an organisation

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters are read from bottom to top

parts.note: a con is a deception or swindle

explanation.surface: Spies use gadgets to hide their trickery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spying' suggests espionage, but here it means simply seeing: single lenses help one spy, or see.
explanation.definitionFit: Single eyeglasses help the wearer see, and to spy is an old word for to see.

clue.text: 18 cops and 1 crazy nut

indicators.note: crazy says the letters are thrown into disorder

parts.note: this cross-reference points to the answer at 18 across, a word for Siamese
the numeral one looks like the letter I

explanation.surface: Thai police and one madman are all nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crazy' works on THAI (the answer to 18), COPS and I, a nine-letter mix.
explanation.definitionFit: This green-kernelled nut comes from a small tree native to western Asia.

clue.text: Father Christmas almost thrown out of capital as a villain

indicators.note: letters thrown out of a word are removed from it

parts.note: Santiago is the capital of Chile

indicators.note: almost means one letter short at the end

parts.note: Santa is Father Christmas

explanation.surface: Father Christmas is nearly expelled from a capital city as a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: SANTA without its last letter is SANT, and taking that out of SANTIAGO, the capital of Chile, leaves the villain.
explanation.definitionFit: He is the scheming villain of Shakespeare's Othello.

clue.text: Siamese cat's close by chair, scratching the covers

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter
scratching off the covers removes the outer letters, leaving the middle

explanation.surface: A Siamese cat is by a chair, clawing the upholstery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Siamese cat' reads as a breed, but 'Siamese' alone is the definition and 'cat' is wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Siam is the old name of Thailand, so something Siamese belongs to that country.

clue.text: American idiot's rally

parts.note: an ass is a fool

explanation.surface: A foolish American is holding a rally.
explanation.definitionFit: To rally supporters is to gather or collect them together.

clue.text: Bent over with large naked body part penetrating

indicators.note: a piece penetrating another goes into it
naked means stripped of its outer letters

parts.note: the chin is a part of the face

explanation.surface: A smutty picture of a big naked body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'naked' strips LARGE to ARG, and CHIN goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Curving over like a bow describes something bent into a curve.

clue.text: Bath drain in which centre pops down

indicators.note: in a down entry, the middle letter drops to the bottom

parts.note: to sap is to drain one's strength

explanation.surface: A bath plug hole into which the middle part falls.
explanation.walkthrough: In SAP the middle letter A moves to the bottom of the down entry. Bath is an English city famous for its Roman baths.
explanation.definitionFit: Bath is an example of a resort town with mineral springs.

clue.text: One Frenchman, following king, in pursuit of Old Pretender

indicators.note: one thing in pursuit of another comes after it

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
M is short for monsieur
post- is a prefix meaning after or following
R is short for rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A French noble follows the king in chasing the Old Pretender, James Stuart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old Pretender' is a historical title, but 'Old' is wordplay and 'Pretender' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretender falsely claims to be someone, as a fraud or charlatan does.

clue.text: Seafood containing a bit of arm buried in the middle

definitions.text: Seafood containing a bit of arm buried in the middle

indicators.note: one piece containing another holds it inside

parts.note: a clam is a seafood shellfish

indicators.note: a bit of the word is its first letter
this takes the central letters of the word

explanation.surface: A seafood dish with a piece of squid arm hidden in it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition too: squid rings include pieces of the squid's arms.
explanation.definitionFit: Squid served as food, usually in battered rings, includes the creature's arms.

clue.text: Game of chance lets one take the other for starters

indicators.note: for starters takes the first letter of each word

explanation.surface: In a game of chance, players take it in turns.
explanation.definitionFit: This lottery-like game of drawn numbers relies on luck alone.

clue.text: Top rate celebrity snubbed and upset the mob

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset turns the letters upside down, so they read upwards

parts.note: A1 means first-rate, with the one as I

indicators.note: snubbed means its end is cut off, like a snub nose

parts.note: fame is celebrity

explanation.surface: A celebrity is snubbed at a top restaurant and the crowd is upset.
explanation.walkthrough: AI plus FAM, from FAME snubbed, is turned upside down by 'upset'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mafia is the organised crime syndicate also known as the Mob.

clue.text: Put in charge after half of hospital's showing stress?

indicators.note: after puts the second piece behind the first
half of means the second half of the word is taken

explanation.surface: An administrator is put in charge after half the hospital shows signs of stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stress' suggests anxiety, but here it is emphasis in print.
explanation.definitionFit: Slanted type is used to give words emphasis on the page.

clue.text: Raise first person among many

indicators.note: a thing among others sits inside them

parts.note: a host is a great many
I is the first-person pronoun

explanation.surface: Lift up the leader among a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: To lift something up, often with a rope or tackle, is to raise it.

clue.text: Concerns of common people voiced by India

indicators.note: voiced means said out loud, so the sound counts and not the spelling

parts.note: folk are ordinary people
India is I in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: An Indian voices the worries of ordinary people.
explanation.definitionFit: Centres of attention are the matters that concern people.

clue.text: Regular appearances of fibroids in circular body part

indicators.note: regular appearances means every other letter is taken

explanation.surface: Fibroids keep showing up in a round part of the body.
explanation.definitionFit: The coloured ring around the pupil of the eye is circular.

clue.text: Ring bell at five past ten to cut short musical or opera

indicators.note: past puts the second piece after the first

parts.note: a bell rings with a dong
ten is written in figures as 1 and 0, read as letters
V is the Roman numeral five

indicators.note: cut short means the last letter is lost

parts.note: Annie is a stage musical

explanation.surface: Someone rings a bell at five past ten to stop a musical show early.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ten' is IO, the figures 1 and 0 read as letters, with V for five after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mozart's opera about the libertine Don Juan.
